records.title: Narrative entry

fields.event: Departed Submarine Base, PEARL HARBOR in accordance with Comsubpac OpOrder No.325-44 of 24 September 1944 in company with SALMON and TRIGGER. Task unit designation 17.19.1. Proceeded to SAIPAN at maximum sustained speed, conducted dives and drills daily.

flags: Qwen read 'OpOrder', Bonsai 'Order'.

fields.event: Passed submarine, probably U.S.S. PAMPANITO, on opposite course, distance 12 miles.
Sighted escort (USS CASSIN) and USS SHARK, USS BLACKFISH, and USS SEADRAGON. All proceeded in company to SAIPAN.

records.title: Narrative entry

fields.event: Moored alongside USS FULTON. Fueled to capacity and accomplished minor voyage repairs. Exchanged one Mk. XVIII-1 torpedo which Submarine Base PEARL had informed us by despatch was defective.

flags: At SAIPAN; the report gives no position. TRIGGER's report has the three boats moored in one nest alongside FULTON (TRIGGER outboard of SILVERSIDES, SALMON outboard of TRIGGER).

records.title: Narrative entry

fields.event: Underway enroute area in company with U.S.S. SALMON. Enroute area conducted daily training dive and fire control drills.

flags: TRIGGER's sailing was delayed a day for repairs to her forward TBT; she followed on 5 October with SEADRAGON.

records.title: Typhoon; Lt. Heidel injured

fields.event: 5-7 October. A typhoon passed us causing heavy seas and at times forcing us to slow to 7 knots to avoid shipping dangerous amounts of water down conning tower hatch and inductions. Lieutenant C.C. HEIDEL received severe head wound when a wave almost knocked him overboard. All times henceforth will be (-)9, (Item), unless otherwise noted.

flags: Headed '5-7 October' with no time; placed on 5 October. Part P counts one head wound resulting in six sick days. Zone I applied from here to the end of the narrative, as the entry states.
No time given; placed at noon GMT on that date.

fields.event: SHIPCON #2. Made radar contact with a group of seven small vessels, probably sampans or a fishing fleet. Closed to 4,000 yards and at this range could barely see one of the vessels. records.title: Gun attack 1

fields.form:
(H) ATTACK DATA.
U.S.S. SILVERSIDES          GUN ATTACK NO. 1.         Patrol No. 11
Time: 1218 - 1638 (I)      15 November, 1944       Lat. 30-02 N. Long. 137-36 E.
Target Data - Damage Inflicted
Damaged:     1 Patrol boat, converted tuna boat type MIS(200T) (EU).
Damage Determined by:
             Saw at least two hits. One hit appeared to start a fire in forecastle which seemed to be extinguished by the next shell which landed close aboard him and showered him with water.
Details of Action
See narrative: Fired 126 rounds of 4" ammunition, 75 rounds of 40 mm and one pan of 20 mm. Average range 6500 yards. Fire was effective as could be expected at this range. Kept hitting
gun range set on T.D.C. and spotted with periscope. Target armed with two 60 mm or possibly 3" guns which we were unable to silence and shot with accuracy at ranges less than 6500 yards. Closest range 4200 yards when we turned away to avoid his fire. We presented a far larger and more vulnerable target than he did.
fields.narrative:
Commenced firing 4" gun at target, range about 7500 yards.

All three submarines commenced firing on signal from pack commander. Range at this time about 7,000 yards.

flags: Transcriber: Addendum page 8A. 'Let.' (Qwen) / 'Lat.' (Bonsai); 'tune' (Qwen) / 'tuna' (Bonsai). TRIGGER's ship contact 2 for the same target: 1255 (I) 11-15-44, 30-05 N 137-38 E, 'small net tender'.
Transcriber: Addendum page 9A.
Narrative entry at 1218 I 15 November 1944 (page 2A) describes this attack; its account is included here.
Narrative entry at 1513 I 15 November 1944 (page 3A) describes this attack; its account is included here.
TRIGGER's addenda: commenced firing at 1512 (I), SILVERSIDES astern of target, STERLET on its starboard quarter and TRIGGER on its port quarter.

fields.event: STERLET dove. Believing that she had sighted a plane, cleared topside and turned away from target with range about 5,000 yards and having expended 58 rounds. For awhile we received his un-divided return fire and he straddled several times. He seemed to have two 60 mm or 3 inch guns that had a maximum range of about 8500 yards, and were fairly accurate at less than 6500 yards. He was playing it cagey and saving his ammunition until the range closed, and was dodging the splashes violently. Several hits were observed during this phrase.
Pack commander sent message to TRIGGER and TAMBOR to join the attack.

records.title: Narrative entry

fields.event: STERLET, having surfaced, reported that she dove because target was straddling her at 7500 yards. Pack commander commenced forming the TRIGGER, SILVERSIDES, and STERLET on a line of bearing preparatory to making a joint attack. TRIGGER while joining up maneuvered radically and reported she had seen a periscope. Possibly this explains why aircraft had not come to rescue of patrol boat, or else his radio is shot away.

flags: TRIGGER's addenda: at 1357 (I) her quartermaster's 'periscope' was later decided to be one of the empty shell cases in the water.

fields.event: With range about 4200 yards, the patrol boat commenced giving us bursts fore and aft, port and starboard, which were close. Cleared 4" crew off deck, reversed course, and fired 40 mm gun until range was outside of his effective range. In this phase 45 rounds of 4" were fired. By now STERLET was out of 5" ammunition, but TRIGGER was still shooting.
Reversed course and headed in again.
Commenced firing again, range about 6500 yards.

records.title: Narrative entry

fields.event: Ceased fire, ammunition low, range about 5500 yards. 23 rounds were fired in this phase, making a total of 126 rounds. Decided to make a submerged torpedo attack. Sent word to STERLET to notify TRIGGER to keep target occupied and we would end around and get in a dusk torpedo attack.

flags: Typed 'submer ed' (both reads).

fields.event: Unable to obtain position before darkness. This patrol boat had probably had over 300 4" and 5" shells fired at him and was damaged by quite a few hits and heading toward the EMPIRE. Pack commander sent message to TRIGGER and STERLET to resume patrol. TRIGGER requested permission to try a night torpedo attack and was given permission.
Searching assigned area. TAMBOR sent out contact report of a patrol boat. Continued to search own assigned area, as doctrine called for only two adjacent boats to attempt contact.

index.text:
### OVERHAUL ADDITIONS
1. Conning tower dooreliminated and after end of conning tower dished out.
2. Installed D.R.T.
3. Moved 40mm from aft position to cigarette deck.
4. Installed V.H.F., TBL modulator, A.P.R., and RBH-2
5. Installed 7 M.C.
6. Installed slotted type S.J. projector and new training motor.
7. Shock mounted cubicle
8. Installed ballistic protection around conning tower.
Transcribed as written. Not sure what "dooreliminated" is supposed to be. Unless they removed a conning tower door. 

Missing week is from the formation of the Saipan sweep group. First part of patrol, then Saipan, then the sweep, then back to Midway.
